The change involves how the values are fetched from the parameterAccessor in the `AbstractDynamoDBQueryCreator.java` file. Previously, the value was directly cast to a String type, which could potentially cause a `ClassCastException` if the value was not of type String.
Now, the change uses `String.valueOf()` method, which would convert the value to a String regardless of its original type. This is a safer approach as it prevents potential runtime exceptions when the value is not a String.

AttributeValue Handling: A significant part of the code changes involve how the system handles `AttributeValue` objects within `ExpressionAttributeValues`. Previously, the value of an `ExpressionAttribute` was directly added as a string to an `AttributeValue`. The updated code now checks if the value can be converted to a Boolean or a Number, and if so, it is added as such to the `AttributeValue`. If not, it is added as a string. This makes the handling of `AttributeValue` more flexible, accommodating different data types and not just strings.
Overall, these changes improve the readability and flexibility of the code, potentially making it easier to maintain and extend in the future.

In this update, several changes were made. Firstly, two directories 'docs/' and 'tmp/' were added to the .gitignore file, which means these folders will be ignored by git and changes in them will not be tracked.
The README.md file was updated to change the link to the XML-based configuration guide. It now points to a markdown file within the 'docs' directory.
In the 'DynamoDBEntityWithHashAndRangeKeyCriteria.java' file, a method was created to handle attribute value conversion. This improves code readability and maintainability by reducing redundancy in the code.
A new file named '_config.yml' was added in the 'docs' directory. This file is used to configure the settings for a Jekyll site, a simple, blog-aware static site generator. This suggests that the project is setting up a Jekyll site for documentation purposes. The configuration file contains site settings such as title, email, description, base URL, twitter username, and Github username. It also includes build settings like the theme and plugins.
Overall, from a business perspective, the project is improving its code structure and setting up a documentation site for better readability and accessibility for users or developers.

The codebase now handles `Date` and `Instant` types more robustly when creating DynamoDB queries. Previously, when mapping expression values, the value was directly converted to a string regardless of its type. Now two new checks have been added: if the value is an instance of `Date` or `Instant`, it is marshalled into an ISO format string using `Date2IsoDynamoDBMarshaller` or `Instant2IsoDynamoDBMarshaller` respectively. This change ensures proper string representation for `Date` and `Instant` types, allowing for accurate querying.
In addition, there has been a change in the location of the `getAttributeValue` method within DynamoDBEntityWithHashAndRangeKeyCriteria.java. However, this is a structural change and doesn't affect the function's behavior or the overall logic.

The changes made to the codebase pertain to handling the test environment and repository methods.
In the User Repository file, a new import statement for `java.util.Date` has been added. This indicates that date-related operations might be performed in the repository.
A significant update was made to the User Pagination Repository. A new method `findByPostCode` was added. This method returns a paginated list of users based on their postal code and the range of joining dates. This allows for more specific and flexible user queries in the application.
In the integration test file `CRUDOperationsIT.java`, a new test case `testFilterWithDateBetween` was added. This test case tests the functionality of filtering users based on their postal code and a date range.
Overall, the update improves the application's ability to filter and retrieve user data.

The changes in this commit are mainly to the documentation (README.md) file of the Spring Data DynamoDB project. Here is what has been updated:
1. The layout for the web page is set and the title is changed to "About". 2. The Maven Central link was changed to point to 'io.github.naderfares' instead of 'io.github.prasanna0586'. This suggests that the project's maintenance has been taken over by a new user named 'naderfares'. 3. The version of the 'spring-data-dynamodb' artifact in the Maven dependency was updated from '6.0.4' to '6.0.9'. 4. The 'Quick Start' section has been simplified and no longer includes detailed instructions on how to set up a DynamoDB configuration, create a DynamoDB entity, create a CRUD repository interface, etc. Instead, it now simply contains instructions on how to add the 'spring-data-dynamodb' dependency to a Maven or Gradle project. 5. The 'Version & Spring Framework compatibility' section's text was updated to be on a single line. 6. The 'History' section has been updated to include the latest forks of the project, showing that it was lastly forked and maintained by 'naderfares' after being handled by 'prasanna0586'. 7. Some sections of the document, like 'Supported Features', 'Demo application', 'More', 'Setup DynamoDB configuration', 'Create a DynamoDB entity', 'Create a CRUD repository interface', 'Create the configuration class', 'And finally write a test client', have been removed, simplifying the document considerably.

The updates in this commit do not impact the functionality of the program. Instead, they alter the code's formatting to improve readability. The change is breaking the line of code that adds an entry to the query expression's attribute values into two lines, making it easier to read and understand. This update was applied in two files: `DynamoDBEntityWithHashAndRangeKeyCriteria.java` and `AbstractDynamoDBQueryCriteria.java`.
